reviews.author: Sandy
reviews.text: First time here. Lovely State Park with beautiful trails. One trail will take you to Butteville Store, which is actually not a store. Very historical with nice lunch menu, and homemade ice cream. Definitely worth the visit. Only 1 mile from Lady Hill Winery via trail.  Delicious wine and setting. So much to explore, especially if you hike or like to walk or ride bikes.  The Park Ranger is very helpful and joyful.  We spent 3 nights and enjoyed everything.  Most of the rv spots are level. Looking forward to returning.

reviews.author: David Hammond
reviews.text: This has to be one of the nicest STATE park we’ve been to. The visitors center is top notch with lots of items for purchase. The facilities throughout are well taken care of. The park is clean and way to navigate.  There is a dump station that is free and has two stations. This is a great park.

reviews.author: Pat Bender
reviews.text: Beautiful park but it needs some work. Trails overgrown, Widowmakers all over ready to fall and flatten people. There was a giant half a tree that had broken off laying on the ground close to the picnic area we had.

reviews.author: j ai
reviews.text: Fun spot for camping. Even though the park is open year round, they close a lot in the winter and only RV sites, yurts and cabins are available for winter camping. Summertime there’s more tent sites and some group tent sites as well. The group tent sites are closer to the river. There is a dock but many signs saying no swimming. The camp hosts are always super nice and helpful and fun to chat with. The rangers are great as well. 💜

reviews.author: Webig93 RV
reviews.text: Love this place.  Great camping, walking, bike riding, birding, and a playground for the kids near the campground.  We come here often as we live nearby, but we love to camp here in our trailer too.  They have educational displays in a few are about the history of the place and early pioneer life.  The VC is nice with cute gift items for sale too.  They also have several group picnic sites that must be reserved.  Perfect for retirement parties or any other occasion.

reviews.author: Kim R
reviews.text: It was really hard to find anything on the tent campsites online, so I'm gonna put it out there. There are six tent sites, lots of parking close by, lots of shade, and really nice size sites. This is a you bring it you haul it out park, but they keep the bathrooms and what few garbage areas they have clean. Showers are free. And clean. Very friendly rangers and on site staff as well.

reviews.author: IKE48
reviews.text: Went to the park for a long walk and was impressed with the beautifully paved path (6 mile to/from path to Butteville). You can turn around at any point. Gorgeous setting. $10 for the day park pass required…worth it.

reviews.author: KATL
reviews.text: Nice campground with spacious and level sites, clean bathrooms, great playground and surrounded by awesome trails! We love Oregon state parks!

reviews.author: 2became1
reviews.text: This is a wonderful park we come to every year. Lots to do near the park. Many activities in the park with a great disc golf course; several paved trails to walk or bike on; and a great field for the dogs to romp in.

reviews.author: mom22sons
reviews.text: Beautiful site off a country road. Good sites some with standard hookups and some with full hookups. Great historical site and information. Bike and walking trails along the Willamette River. Good showers and flush toilets. Close to place to sightsee like a pioneer cemetery, old town, large town and visitors center with museum. Great recycle area and dump station.

reviews.author: dan a
reviews.text: If you show up late for a Yurt rental, things will get hectic real fast! The information on their website conflicts with their actual practices, which is exactly what the Ranger (Kyle Parker) told me, so don't expect a refund or anything like that if you show up and your rental is locked. This place is run by people who barely work, so when something comes up, they're grossly unprepared / incompetent.

reviews.author: JenHOregon
reviews.text: Went in September, had a yurt. This time of year, nothing is green. Pretty hot during summer. The wasps were out of control! Could not sit on bench outside, for sure could not eat outside. This was an issue because it was 90 out and the yurt was a sauna! The bathrooms did not have trash and were kept up, but they are what you would find at a rest stop. Too scared to even use the shower. Lots of walking/biking trails. Cute small park for kids to play. They had Frisbee golf, but there is a lot of people who actually play with the professional equipment, so we didn't play with our lame frisbee's.. Both park hosts were very kind and helpful. State park employees not friendly at all. Last night there a state park employee flew up on her golf cart at 7:45 and said 'you heard about the fire ban right?" as she was zip tying our fire pit. Like how in the world would I have heard that??? This was the worst camping trip I have had and I have decides I will stick to KOA's or equivalent from now on.

reviews.author: D m
reviews.text: Nice sites, showers & bathroom clean. Wood $7, $37 for power sute. $10 reservation fee this year. Weekend was complete full. T-mobile worked good and hot spoted netflix onto roku TV fine. Not too far off 5 freeway. Nice kids playground. 😎

reviews.author: KFE
reviews.text: Beautiful Park, not far off of I-5. A loop has smaller, more tight sites, Only a few fit big rigs. B loop is newer with more private sites and more big rig friendly. 6 Primitive Yurts and 6 Cabins available. Close to shopping in Newberg, 40 minutes to downtown Portland. Good att, others not so much. Reservation only

reviews.author: Ann
reviews.text: Nice big sites, great trails and play areas for the kids - we are planning a winter trip after staying for a week in the summer too. Bring the bikes for the family too!

reviews.author: Ron
reviews.text: We stayed here Oct 17 thru 21, 2018. We won't return nor will we suggest it to our friends. Every morning the same three run down trailers would cruise through the park numerous times. It was a little unnerving to leave our RV unattended during the day to enjoy the surrounding area. While we were at our RV the people in the trailers would yell four letter obscenities at their kids and they allowed their dogs to bark which was very annoying. I walked our dog in the designated dog area in B loop at 5:45 a.m. and one of the trailers was parked in the nearby parking lot which had a sign stating "no camping". We won't be returning. I think it is sad that the park is being taken over by the homeless.

reviews.author: WHR NXT
reviews.text: Love, love, love this campground. We stayed at 7 state parks in Oregon over 6 weeks, and this was my favorite. Our site was B34, and an end site, so we had a large side lot for our toddler to run around in. There is a natural playground in the campground which was a hit. The best part of the park for us was the 4 miles of paved (relatively flat) bike paths. If you go right for 2 miles from the campground you ride through old growth forests and can visit the oldest, continuously operated store in Oregon. If you go left for 2 miles, you ride through the forest, the oak grove, prairies, and then forest with 100 year old Sequoias. Their visitor center was one of the nicest we have seen at a State Park, and had a kitchen garden and heirloom orchard behind it, representative of what settlers had. Our site just had water and electric, and was not very shady, overall A loop had more shade, but the sites were closer together there. Great park, can't wait to return.

reviews.author: 2FulltimersinaFifth
reviews.text: We stayed 2-weeks at this state park, when visiting the Portland area. We really enjoyed the natural beauty, the walking trail along the Willamette River and the proximity to wine country and downtown Portland. All of the Park Rangers and campground hosts were extremely nice. Many of the sites in Loop B are big rig friendly (i.e., fewer trees and typically longer sites than in Loop A). We had no issues with Verizon data coverage (mifi, no booster), but received much better cell coverage when using AT&T (compared to Verizon). We enjoyed our stay here and look forward to returning in the future.
